title: Dangling timeout IDs after replay with inflight timeouts

evidence.quote: const at = (fn: () => void, ms: number) => { idsRef.current.push(setTimeout(fn, ms)) }

const step = () => {
      if (i <= text.length) { t.textContent = text.slice(0, i); i++; idsRef.current.push(setTimeout(step, 48)) }

reasoning: The typewriter function at line 198 recursively schedules timeouts and pushes IDs to idsRef.current inside the timeout callback. If clearAll() is called while typewriter is mid-execution, already-scheduled but not-yet-fired typewriter steps will still fire and push new IDs after idsRef.current has been cleared, causing those IDs to never be cleared.
reproduction: Start demo, trigger replay() during the typewriter animation. The typewriter step callbacks that were already scheduled will execute after clearAll() and add new timeout IDs that won't be tracked.
recommendation: Add a cancellation flag that typewriter checks before scheduling the next step, or track a generation ID to ignore stale callbacks.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests exist. This requires timing-sensitive testing to trigger replay during active typewriter animation and verify all timeouts are properly cancelled.
suggestedRegressionTest: Unit test: start typewriter, immediately call clearAll, advance timers, verify no new timeout IDs are added to idsRef.current.
minimumFixScope: Lines 195-202 in src/src/pages/MRODemo.tsx - add cancellation token to typewriter closure
